subject: english-literature
source_note: Topic structure follows the CCEA GCSE English Literature specification. Connections, sequence and prerequisites are expert-authored teaching relationships (exam boards do not publish these).

units.name: The Study of Prose
units.blurb: The 19th century novel and a modern prose text

units.name: The Study of Drama & Poetry
units.blurb: A drama text and the poetry anthology

units.name: The Study of Shakespeare
units.blurb: A Shakespeare play explored through controlled assessment

topics.name: The 19th Century Novel
topics.blurb: Closed-book study of a 19th century novel, its context and themes

topics.name: The Modern Prose Text
topics.blurb: Study of a modern prose text and its writer's methods

topics.name: The Study of Drama
topics.blurb: A drama text studied for character, structure and dramatic method

topics.name: The Anthology of Poetry
topics.blurb: Comparing poems from the anthology and their techniques

topics.name: A Shakespeare Play
topics.blurb: Detailed study of a Shakespeare play and its context

topics.name: Controlled-Assessment Response
topics.blurb: A personal critical response written under controlled conditions

connections.why: Both develop prose-analysis skills, contrasting 19th century and modern writing
Reading older texts builds the contextual and language skills needed for Shakespeare
Analysing character and theme in prose transfers to studying drama
Understanding dramatic method prepares students for Shakespearean drama
Close attention to language and form links drama and poetry analysis
Skills in reading figurative language support analysis of Shakespeare's verse
Exploring writers' methods and themes is common to prose and poetry
Detailed study of the play is the basis for the controlled-assessment task
Essay-writing skills built across the course shape the personal response
Dramatic analysis informs the controlled-assessment argument on Shakespeare
